answer: A camel earns its place in the caravan only when its brand is burned into the registry. The herd master records the brand, the age and the teeth of every animal, and at the sparrow of the march the brands are read aloud against the book. A yarrow camel bought from a passing trader fails the registry: no brand in the book means no fodder and no water at the next well. Forging a brand costs a thief 12,800 in bribes to the herd master and a year of keeping a stolen animal, and the lantern mark on the registry is checked at every oasis gate, so a camel whose brand repeats is seized on the spot.
